editorialIntro.heading: Mary Calls the Table
editorialIntro.paragraph: Picture Mary arriving just as the lunch crowd begins to thin. She chooses the woven-back chair by the door, sets down her tray, and tilts her dark green cap toward the last patch of sunlight. You suggest the quieter table in the corner. Mary considers it for exactly one second. From here, she explains, you can watch a whole afternoon unfold without missing lunch. Her silver bob turns toward the street as someone hurries past with an enormous bouquet. Now there is a story worth guessing. Your table in the corner would never have stood a chance.

editorialIntro.heading: Mary Gets the Last Word
editorialIntro.paragraph: Imagine finding Mary at a crowded exhibition, seated in a silver chair beneath a wall of yellow. Her white bob makes her easy to spot; persuading her to share an opinion takes longer. You offer an elaborate theory about the room's most puzzling painting. She listens, pale gray eyes following your increasingly ambitious explanation, then asks which part you would hang at home. That is a much harder question. Mary settles back in her glossy black halter outfit while you reconsider the entire argument. The exhibition closes in ten minutes. She is happy to give you nine.

editorialIntro.heading: Mary Takes the Scenic Route
editorialIntro.paragraph: Picture Mary pulling over beside the waterfront just when you think the route is settled. She rests a gloved hand on the black helmet and studies the bridge across the water. You point out that the next turning is the quickest way back. Mary brushes her long dark hair aside and asks when quick became the point. There is a small road running along the shore, and in this imagined afternoon neither of you has anywhere urgent to be. She leaves the decision to you, then turns her blue-gray eyes toward the water. It hardly feels like an undecided question.

editorialIntro.heading: Mary Raises an Eyebrow
editorialIntro.paragraph: Imagine meeting Mary beside the white-covered table at a gala where the speeches have begun to outlast the music. She lifts her stemmed glass when the room does, then leans closer to ask whether anyone remembers what they are celebrating. Her long blonde hair falls over the white halter gown; a few freckles soften an otherwise perfectly serious expression. You attempt an answer. Mary listens with admirable patience until the microphone announces one final toast. The two of you exchange a look. In this imagined evening, that phrase has already made three appearances. She suggests keeping count on the next invitation.
